messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text:
**Blubber Magazine - 2013 Regular Season Cumming To Close - Take It Up With Cocksinsun Volume 126**

*The 2013 season, aka S18, is scheduled to turn into a pumpkin in roughly 3 days, capping off a long and dull stretch of nhl95 hockey.  The lack of excitement surrounding the World National is unmistakably as low as it’s ever been, and over the past few weeks, we’ve unleashed our interns to delve into just why the league seems impotent.  There are some seemingly obvious answers, namely, the regular season is too long.  Others may be far less obvious….Here’s what they came back with…*

__#1) The regular season is too long….  __
90 days….. NINETY for a regular season of 56 games.  This once proud league, ripe with excitement to be able to relive our glory days, used to have seasons > 80 games and the timeframe was shorter.  Back then, we didn’t have nearly the amount of tech perks that we have today….Streaming was few and far between, if at all, no websites and delayed box scores.  Have all the new features played a part in reducing excitement overall?  Not likely….

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text:
__#2)  It’s the same teams in the playoffs every season…. __
This doesn’t seem like it would be the major catalyst, but could impact the initiative of those perennially towards the bottom with red squares.  I guess that could be understandable after double digit seasons.  More holistically, the league is arguably as competitive as it’s ever been.  Over the past few years, there’s been a number of different (and new) champions.  A handful of Shitty Bill “regulars” have put themselves in the mix for a Brule birth, most notably Betty Ford (clinched) and MNYoda (bubble).  Does this give teams below them hope?  Not likely…So yes, it is the same teams every year to a certain extent.  I personally thought this league would be at more players by now, with likely a champions/relegation league type situation, but it’s not.  That’s too bad, but blame the marketing department….

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text:
__#3) The regular season starts when there’s a week left…__
This is a problem, but worse than that, it’s been a problem for a long time.  Teams shouldn’t be able to wait until the end and crowbar in 90% of their season into a week.  Yes people get busy, have personal things going on, yada yada….That’s fine, but there’s obviously a group that thinks it’s cute to take this approach, and while the playful banter is funny for a minute, it does get old.  So we here at BM do feel this is a major factor in the lack of excitement, but it’s unlikely to bring change anytime soon.  Would a midseason marker help, to at least force teams to get to the midway point in a reasonable amount of time?  Maybe….probably??  But after 40+ seasons, things will probably just continue as they are.  Secondary to draining the excitement is the fact that this approach, due to lack of integrity or consequences, leads to fake games being submitted.  On the surface, this may seem like a fair approach;  2 teams that weren’t able to play just submit two ties or a split, etc.  The problem is there’s a few in the World National that do not take this approach, and would just take the penalties that come with not finishing.  So the innocence of submitting fake games, after being unable to carve out 20 minutes a week, does impact other teams, and likely teams that need some help.

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text:
__#4) Maybe it’s just run it’s course…..__
Not gonna lie, what’s going on over on the 94 server is next level amazing!  Does the World National need to follow their lead to stay afloat?  A few weeks ago, my answer would have been no, but I’m quickly questioning it more and more.  Given what this league has ~ decent number of streamers, BSB, live standings/stats, podcasts, etc ~ it wouldn’t seem necessary to duplicate (we can’t), or beg them to let us in, but I think it’s quickly becoming something we should look into.  It just feels like something needs to be done.  

I think this league has been around for over 5 years now, and it’s been amazing.  Change is always inevitable, and perhaps change is what the World National needs.  In 5 years, we’ve never surpassed the max number of allowed teams.  Growth is necessary IMO to keep things fresh and exciting.  Otherwise, we only have numbers 1-3 above to talk about for 3 months a year.  

So where do we go from here?  I don’t know….Be sure to drop a comment and smash that like button if you enjoyed the content….



**Brian Cocksinsun is a Senior Writer for Blubber Magazine and his parents are somehow happy together and still attend family picnics**
